messages:
lee (customer): hi, running into intermittent truncated JSON when using streaming mode. curl shows stream cut off mid-object. request-id: r-0a1b2c3d; region: eu-west-1. sample response (ends abruptly):

```
data: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...many tokens...\"}}, {\"delta\":{\"content\":\"more...\"}}]\ndata: {\"id\":\"resp-abc\", \"object\":\"chat.completion.chunk\", \"finish_reason\": null
```

connection just closes, no final `data: [DONE]` or closing brace. happening ~1-2x / 50 streams.

maria: sorry about that — we'll take a look. can you paste the curl command and response headers? also any intermediate proxy (CF/NGINX) in front?

lee (customer): curl command below. i'm going through Cloudflare spectrum -> our internal proxy -> redwood endpoint.

```bash
curl -v --no-buffer \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\n  --data '{\"model\":\"x\",\"stream\":true,\"prompt\":\"long...\"}' \\n  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream\"
```

response headers (truncated):
```
HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC
server: redwood-gw
```

raj: thanks — two quick checks: 1) can you repro by resolving the origin IP directly (bypass CF) with `--resolve`? 2) try adding `Connection: close` to the request to see if keepalive is involved.

lee (customer): tried --resolve to origin IP and it *seems* more stable but still fails for very long streams (>2k tokens). with `Connection: close` it cuts less often. attaching a tcpdump snippet that shows final FIN from an intermediate hop about ~30s before final event is streamed.

sre_oliver: intermediate FIN from upstream proxy -> likely keepalive socket being recycled while heavy tail streaming still ongoing. some proxies will cork or reset idle connections if there's long tail without traffic. two mitigations to try: reduce server-side idle timeout or increase heartbeat frequency from client (send tiny keepalive chunks), or send an explicit final sentinel chunk periodically.

eng_anna: we can add a server-side mitigation: always emit a very small noop event (`data: {\"_\":\"heartbeat\"}\n\n`) every 8-10s during long streams so intermediates see activity. not ideal but low-risk. i'll create a small patch to the streaming runtime to emit periodic flushes for streams >1s intervals.

maria: i've filed SUPPORT-1123 and attached lee's tcpdump + request-id + curl snippet. priority: high. temporary workaround recommended: add `Connection: close` or client-side keepalive (send `\n`-only SSE heartbeats) for now.

lee (customer): thanks — i'll try the `Connection: close` test and implement a client heartbeat. will report back tomorrow. one more Q: any chance you can add a server-side detection so we return a clear error if stream terminates without final object (so clients can retry)?

eng_anna: yes, that's on the roadmap for the runtime — we'll return a non-200 telemetry marker to indicate `stream_incomplete` and emit a structured `error` event where possible. will track in ENG-STREAM-58.

support-bot: [automated] Ticket SUPPORT-1123 created and linked to ENG-STREAM-58. Assigned: eng_anna.

maria: pinging again if anything else, otherwise we'll keep the ticket and follow up once eng has the patch. :thumbsup:
